headline: Coda reallocates flow-matching VLA inference compute to a learned endpoint correction
summary: The authors introduce Coda, a learned endpoint correction for frozen flow-matching vision-language-action policies. On RoboTwin 2.0 simulation, they report that five-step Coda raises task success from 71.64% to 74.68% over a matched five-step baseline across 50 Easy tasks, while reducing measured model-forward latency 30.2% against the default ten-step policy. A separate 13-task comparison reports a 5.69-point success gain at nearly equal latency, and an implementation on frozen SmolVLA reports a two-step gain from 60.8% to 69.4%. The paper reports no clear average gain on its visual-randomization Hard protocol; latency excludes communication and physical execution, and no real-robot evaluation or independent reproduction was conducted.
